card.name: Hedging words in warning statements
card.fires_on: Small hedging or linking words such as some, always, associated, due, for in warning-section sentences saying an effect has been reported or linked with a drug. They come just before the named adverse effect.

modes.label: Qualifiers of how many
modes.description: Words like some or always that limit how widely a reported effect applies.
modes.example: In clinical trials, the occurrence of somnolence has been reported in<< some>> patients (6 of 853

modes.label: Linking verbs and prepositions
modes.description: Words such as associated, due or for that link a drug to a possible adverse effect.
modes.example: Lapatinib has been<< associated>> with interstitial lung disease and pneumon

card.writes: Promotes hedged, qualifying words such as slightly and 存在一定 (a certain degree exists), pushing toward cautious phrasing.
card.plain: It fires on softening words in warnings that say a side effect has been reported in some patients or linked to a drug.
